rows.claim: Asad says materialists deny resurrection, thereby denying God's creative power and, ultimately, His existence.
rows.anchor: Since they are enmeshed in a materialistic outlook on life, such people deny - as the sequence shows - all possibility of resurrection

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means a thing desired or to be desired, hence a sensible course of action.
rows.anchor: Lit., "a thing desired" or "to be desired", i.e., a sensible course of action.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad reads "faiths of latter days" as faiths prevalent in his own time, alluding to Christianity's Trinity and other beliefs in multiple or incarnate divine powers, including Hinduism's triad.
rows.anchor: I.e., "in any of the faiths prevalent in our days": an oblique reference to Christianity and its dogma of the Trinity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form nazzala conveys gradual, continuing revelation, so Asad uses the present tense for God's ongoing bestowal from on high.
rows.anchor: The verbal form nazzala indicates both gradualness and continuity in the process of divine revelation

rows.speaker: Zamakhshari
rows.claim: Asad prefers Zamakhshari's contextual sense of mathani as statements of truth repeated in manifold forms.
rows.anchor: mathani (p1. of mathna), as explained by Zamakhshari in his commentary on the above verse

rows.speaker: Razi
rows.claim: Razi offers the alternative that mathani means pairing statements, reflecting the Qur'an's many polarities such as command and prohibition, reward and punishment, and light and darkness.
rows.anchor: Another possible meaning, preferred by Razi, is "pairing its statements", i.e., referring to the polarity stressed in all Qur'anic teachings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the Qur'an's inner consistency, Asad points readers to 4:82 and 25:32 and their notes.
rows.anchor: As regards the inner consistency of the Qur'an, see also 4:82 and 25:32, as well as the corresponding notes.

rows.anchor: Or: "He guides therewith whomever He wills", either of these two formulations being syntactically correct.

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad refers readers to his note 4 on 14:4 for this statement about divine misguidance.
rows.anchor: See note 4 on 14:4.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protecting oneself with one's face is an idiom meaning that the person has nothing whatever with which to shield himself.
rows.anchor: an idiomatic phrase implying that the person concerned has nothing whatever with which to protect himself.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those worshipped beside God include false deities, living or dead saints, and abstract powers or values such as wealth, status, racial preeminence, and self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: This relates not merely to false deities, but also to saints alive or dead, and even to certain abstract concepts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad says the godless magnify the need to heed these imaginary powers and frighten themselves and others with fears of practical harm if they are ignored.
rows.anchor: The godless always stress the supposed necessity of paying attention to all these imaginary forces and values

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim of being given prosperity by one's "knowledge" means attributing it to one's own ability and shrewdness.
rows.anchor: Lit., "knowledge" - i.e., "my prosperity is due to my own ability and shrewdness": see the first sentence of 28:78 and the corresponding note.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad contrasts Qarun's version of this boast in 28:78 with the earlier-revealed present passage, where it characterizes humanity generally; 7:189-190 show the same tendency in connection with parenthood.
rows.anchor: in the present instance - which is by far the earlier in the chronology of Qur'anic revelation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence of suffering fell due as the ineluctable consequence of the deniers' unrepented sinning.
rows.anchor: as an ineluctable consequence of their unrepented sinning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad inserts "alleged" to preserve the obvious sarcasm in Pharaoh's remark about Moses invoking his Sustainer.
rows.anchor: My interpolation of the word "alleged" is necessitated by the obvious sarcasm of Pharaoh's remark.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad compares this believing man with the believer in the parable at 36:20-27, especially note 15.
rows.anchor: Cf. the parable of the believer in 36:20-27 and, in particular, the corresponding note 15.

words: وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًۭا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad reads the believer's argument as saying Moses' convincing message itself proves he is not spiritually self-destructive through a false claim to divine inspiration.
rows.anchor: Thus, the anonymous believer spoken of here argues that the message brought by Moses is so convincing that, by itself, it is a proof

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers are angelic forces watching over sinners' suffering in the hereafter; Asad suggests they may allegorize the belated awakening of sinners' conscience.
rows.anchor: perhaps an allegory of the belated awakening of the latters' conscience.

rows.speaker: classical commentators
rows.claim: Classical commentators take the keepers' reply as a refusal to intercede, effectively telling the doomed sinners to pray for themselves if they can.
rows.anchor: According to the classical commentators, this answer implies no more than a refusal on the part of the "keepers of hell" to intercede

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad instead reads "pray, then" as telling sinners to invoke the false worship objects and values to which they once attributed a share in divinity and see whether those can help.
rows.anchor: we have here an indirect allusion to the sinners erstwhile, blasphemous devotion to false objects of worship and false values

words: وَمَا دُعَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad's reading is supported by the next clause: the deniers' prayers were deluded in earthly life, whereas such delusions have vanished by Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: This interpretation finds support in the next sentence, which speaks of the delusion (dalal) inherent in the prayers of "those who deny the truth"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When thumma joins parallel statements without a necessary time sequence, it functions as a simple conjunction and can be rendered "and".
rows.anchor: it has the function of a simple conjunction, and may be rendered as "and".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad identifies dukhan as gas, evidently hydrogen, which physicists regard as the primal element from which material particles evolve.
rows.anchor: a gas - evidently hydrogen gas, which physicists regard as the primal element from which all material particles of the universe have evolved and still evolve

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For sama in its cosmic sense, Asad points to his note 20 on 2:29.
rows.anchor: For the meaning of the term sama ("sky" or "skies" or "heaven") in its cosmic connotation, see note 20 on 2:29.

rows.speaker: Zamakhshari
rows.claim: Zamakhshari calls "willingly or unwillingly" a figurative expression for the inevitability of God's almighty will.
rows.anchor: Zamakshari adds: "If I am asked about the meaning of [the words] 'willingly or unwillingly', I say that it is a figurative expression

rows.speaker: Razi
rows.claim: Razi connects this prohibition and call to worship God with the earlier phrase about calling people unto God in 41:33.
rows.anchor: This, according to Razi, connects with the phrase "calling (one's fellow-men] unto God" in verse 33 above.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this context, adoration means ascribing real power to something.
rows.anchor: to ascribe real power (which is the meaning of "adoration" in this context) to anything created

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is the cause and source of existence; created phenomena are signs of His power, so attributing real power to any created phenomenon, force, circumstance, or idea is unreasonable and blasphemous.
rows.anchor: God is the sole cause and source of all that exists; and whatever exists is but a wondrous sign of His creative power.
